summary: Canada Lookouts dates an 80-foot steel tower with an octagon cab to 1931 at Lost Channel and reports fires seen from it in 1933; no later history of the tower was found.

facts.design: Light steel tower with an octagon cab

events.note: Canada Lookouts dates the erection of an 80-foot light steel tower with an octagon cab to 1931.
A 6 September 1933 Ottawa Journal item, as reproduced on the index, reports fires sighted from the lookout tower at Lost Channel.

notes_for_editor: The 1931 build date and the 1933 fire sighting both come from the Canada Lookouts index alone, and the index's own quote from the Ottawa Journal reads 'half as dozen', probably a typo for 'half a dozen'; the story avoids the number. The index's Lost Channel page carries a 'Severn River' heading that no source explains. The record coordinates (44.8948, -79.644) do not match the Wikipedia article's coordinates (45.896074 N, 80.319434 W, from its map link), which sit in Parry Sound District, so the record's position should be checked before any map use. Mill fire dates conflict: Wikipedia says a 1928 fire consumed the mill, while Ghost Town Pix says a fire damaged it in 1930. The story mentions neither, because it does not need the mill fire. No source read ties the tower to the mill site, so the story does not link them. No later history, fate or present state of the tower was found.
